associationClusters.association: Steel/coal profitability recovered as capacity was removed and industrial demand stayed firm. This is the archetypal known-cycle control: search for direct earnings conversion, but label it known_cycle unless a genuinely new profit stream emerges inside a company.

Aluminium moved from generic overcapacity policy into actual illegal-capacity shutdowns large enough to affect national supply. Map direct producers, power-cost structures and downstream pass-through; distinguish already-known commodity repricing from new company-specific earnings pools.

Large-scale environmental inspections made legal operating capacity, monitoring/compliance equipment and cleaner-process capability scarcer. Search after the hub signal for companies where environmental enforcement creates a new order stream or a newly material compliant-capacity advantage, rather than simply higher commodity prices.

Factory output and infrastructure-related activity repeatedly beat expectations. Search for equipment or automation businesses only where orders/backlog show an incremental company conversion; do not infer a generic machinery long.

Exports/imports remained strong while iron-ore imports eased even as steel prices encouraged mills to raise output. Test whether margins shifted inside the steel value chain rather than simply following headline production.

The RMB appreciated about 1.69% in August. Map companies with material USD liabilities or imported input costs and RMB revenues, while screening exporters as potential losers. This is a macro cost-transfer control rather than an emerging-profit-pool thesis unless a previously minor exposure becomes material.

Capacity-reduction policy expanded into shipbuilding, where excess capacity was severe. Search for surviving yards with improving order quality/pricing or restructuring-derived profit pools, but reject if demand remains too weak for earnings conversion.
